solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High point in cold capital city close to crucifix

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Lima is the capital city of Peru

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of crucifix

explanation.surface: A travel note about reaching a peak beside a crucifix in a chilly capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the culmination or peak of something, its highest point.

clue.text: Quickly slice thick piece of meat

parts.note: to chop is to cut or slice
a chop is a thick cut of meat, often with a rib

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut a pork chop fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exclamation urging speed, meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Publication for children

definitions.meaning: an edition of a magazine or newspaper
offspring, as in died without legitimate heirs

explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a periodical, and issue also means offspring in law.

clue.text: Lab gear is reassembled for this school subject

indicators.note: reassembled means taken apart and put back together differently

explanation.surface: Lab equipment rebuilt for a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics taught as a school subject.

clue.text: Engraver settled in Dorset (Chertsey-born)

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A craftsman living in Dorset who was born in the Surrey town of Chertsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of Dorset and the start of Chertsey. Dorset is an English county and Chertsey a town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher engraves designs into metal plates with acid, a kind of engraver.

clue.text: Tons delivered with shellfish may make one blink

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for ton or tons
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A huge load of seafood arriving that might make someone blink.
explanation.definitionFit: To twinkle can mean to wink or blink the eyes, as in an instant's flicker.

clue.text: Dependants causing irritation between husband and his boy?

indicators.note: between means the middle piece sits between the other two

parts.note: a man's boy is his son
anger is irritation or annoyance

explanation.surface: Family friction when a father and son quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are people who attach themselves to others for gain, sponging dependants.

clue.text: Find fish round it under end of pier

indicators.note: round says the fish word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places this piece below the other
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching a fish swimming around something below the end of a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like a verb but is the noun definition; in a down clue 'under' stacks the pieces, and 'round' wraps the fish around both.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is a rare or valuable discovery, so a rarity is a good find.

clue.text: Go-go-goes wild for fruit, locally

indicators.note: going wild suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dancer's go-go moves turn frantic, apparently for the sake of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A GOOSEGOG is a regional British word for a gooseberry; 'locally' flags the dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosegog is a northern and dialect English name for the gooseberry, a fruit.

clue.text: Top chess player, magnificent teacher

parts.note: grand means magnificent or splendid
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A champion chess player who is also a superb instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmaster is the highest title awarded to chess players by FIDE.

clue.text: Take no notice of one rig at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Advice to disregard a single oil rig out in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention, the plain verb sense.

clue.text: Top expert receiving millions

indicators.note: receiving means the word for expert takes in the other letter

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person, an expert
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A leading specialist being paid a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the summit or peak of achievement, the very top.

clue.text: Gloomy former PM in suburban area of London

parts.note: black can mean dismal or gloomy, as in a black mood
Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A dejected ex-Prime Minister spotted in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackheath is a district of south-east London; Edward Heath was a Conservative Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackheath is a residential district in south-east London, an example of such a suburb.

clue.text: Opera songs by padre, rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged tells us to put these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A chaplain reorders the hymns to make an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: SONGS BY PADRE has exactly the twelve letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Porgy and Bess is George Gershwin's 1935 folk opera, one example of the form.

clue.text: Top garden in resort — sponsor required

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sorting the letters again

explanation.surface: The finest garden in a holiday town needs a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for its upbringing.

clue.text: Complete ring coming from cigar

parts.note: perfect means complete or absolute, as in a perfect stranger
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A whole smoke ring rising from a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecto is a thick cigar tapered at both ends.

clue.text: Blunder badly, leave out a family (German)

parts.note: to drop something is to leave it out
a clan is an extended family group

explanation.surface: Making a serious mistake by excluding a German family from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a clanger is a British idiom for making a conspicuous, embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Working with a northern fellow never-endingly

parts.note: on means working or operating, as a machine is on
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Toiling alongside a man from the north without ever stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on means continuing without stopping, endlessly.

clue.text: Allegiance shown the Tudors, say, when changing sides?

indicators.note: changing sides swaps the right abbreviation for the left one

parts.note: the Tudors were a royal house, an example of royalty

explanation.surface: The loyalty shown to the Tudor monarchs, by turncoats.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left, so 'changing sides' swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is faithful allegiance to a sovereign or cause.

clue.text: Charge way over the odds for wool

definitions.meaning: the woolly coat shorn from a sheep

explanation.surface: Overpricing a woollen garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is to swindle or overcharge someone, and a fleece is a sheep's wool coat.

clue.text: Agreeable remark made by labourers' leader surrounded by body of rustics

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first letter inside the group word

parts.note: the peasantry is the class of country folk taken as a body

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friendly comment from a farmhands' foreman among the villagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite, light remark made in conversation.

clue.text: One seeking damages losing simple argument

indicators.note: losing means the second word is taken away from the first

parts.note: a plaintiff brings a civil suit, usually to claim damages
plain means simple or unadorned

explanation.surface: A litigant loses a straightforward dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor argument.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery I found among Scarlett's property

indicators.note: found among says the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: Tara is Scarlett O'Hara's plantation in Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A gem discovered in Scarlett's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarlett O'Hara, heroine of Gone with the Wind, owns the plantation Tara.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Key on completion

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the end of something is its completion

explanation.surface: A key being turned once the job is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend on a map or chart is the key explaining its symbols.

clue.text: Trust one to feed new cleaner

indicators.note: to feed means the single letter goes into the other letters
new suggests the word is remade into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Relying on a recently hired cleaner to cook a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes RELANCE from CLEANER, and 'to feed' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence or confidence placed in someone, the same sense as trust.

clue.text: Carry on with former nurse

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Continuing a relationship with a nurse one used to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to prolong or continue something further.

clue.text: Energetic type held back by so many distractions

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lively worker kept from getting on by too many interruptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' also hides the selection: the run sits across sO MANY Distractions and is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a figurative term for a tirelessly energetic, forceful person.
